Thanksgiving dinner got cheaper three years in a row. This year? The streak just broke.
A classic feast for ten hit a record sixty-four dollars in 2022. Then it fell three years straight, to fifty-five eighteen in 2025.
The Farm Bureau's new survey says 2026 costs fifty-eight sixty-three. Up more than six percent.
The turkey. A sixteen-pound bird is twenty-three sixty-eight, up ten percent. Cranberries, up almost nine. Milk, up eight and a half.
And where you live matters. The Northeast pays sixty-one fifty-seven. The South, fifty-four thirty-three.
Turkey or the sides: what are you cutting this year? Tell me in the comments.
